title: Is the Wheel Strategy Actually Worth It?
text: That's what people say, because when you sell a cash secured put, you collect a premium, and then if you get assigned, people will say, "Well, you get it at a price that you wanted, and you get paid to do it." The problem with that, as a lot of you know, is conditions change. The point that you might have been happy taking assignment might change in the future depending on what's going on in the world. That tends to be a problem for people. The next thing is you get paid to sell your shares, because when you sell a call, you would sell your shares if it's in the money at your strike price, and you collect a premium there. But again, the issue with that is we're capping our upside, so you're missing a lot of upside profit potential. It's not all bad. And what I'm emphasizing here is just being able to look at a strategy objectively and saying, "These are the things that are good about this thing. These are the things that kind of aren't ideal. And is there a way to help me improve it?"
